knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A visible crack and loose beading are defects. The panel is recorded as a defect, marked as held and reported in writing. Calling it safe because it is at ground level overstates what was checked.
A possible hidden crack is an unknown. The learner records it as unknown and refers it, and does not press or tap the glass to test it.
Sealant work is out of scope for this course. The request is recorded and referred, and a price is not quoted on the spot.
A cavity that cannot be seen is an unknown until a competent person has assessed it. Recording it as sound, compliant or rotten claims a finding the survey did not make.
The survey records what was visible from a safe position. It does not certify the glazing or frame, and a signature does not change that.

practicalCriteria: The learner numbers each pane and frame in the scope on the survey sheet or sketch.
The learner records visible defects and unknowns in separate columns.
The learner marks any cracked or unstable panel as held and does not clean it.
The learner records the survey date, surveyor, supervisor and weather, and states the survey limits in writing.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately on a real or photographed survey sheet. The knowledge pass is not practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Survey sheet with numbered panels, date, surveyor and weather
Defect list with photographs showing the panel number
Unknowns list with the reason each item could not be verified
Hold or referral record with the person notified
stopWorkCriteria: A pane is cracked through, or a panel rattles or moves in its frame.
The learner presses or leans on glass to test it.
The learner agrees to repair sealant or glazing during the survey.
The learner records a panel or frame as safe or compliant.
